newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest grains futures market pauses for breath.
newsitem.headline: Budapest grains futures market pauses for breath.

text.p: Most grains futures prices remained steady amid minimal turnover on the Budapest Commodity Exchange on Monday in the absence of strong guidance from either international markets or the weather, traders said.
"The market was very quiet today after last week's considerable price drops and significant turnover," said Imre Uzonyi of brokerage Swap.
He added that Chicago prices moved very little on Friday and current weather conditions were of little consequence to the approaching wheat harvest.
"We have already had enough rain and the weather will again become an important factor only during harvesting," he said.
Uzonyi expected prices to move sideways over the next days, unless fresh players -- like producers, mills or international buyers -- enter the market.
Maize futures rose 100 forints per tonne for October to 20,350, milling wheat dropped 300 forints for July, 10 for August and rose 30 for December.
Feed wheat eased for October and Sunflower seed finished lower for November.
Turnover dropped to 229.9 million forints or 477 lots from Friday's 1.1 billion forints or 2,468 lots.
Milling wheat was the most traded, accounting for 272 lots of the day's turnover.
